proposition: Install RentOK and a PG owner's month stops being an obstacle course: verification, rent, skips, reconciliation and complaints come back as rows already cleared.

board.style_line: 9:16 vertical, 16-bit side-scrolling video-game frame, flat pixel art with a two-pixel dark outline and four-colour shading and no gradients, one hard key from screen-left, the whole world graded down to dusty concrete greys and faded ochre with cyan #03FFF1 the only saturated colour anywhere, straight-on locked game camera unless a move is named —
board.negative_line: — no text, no letters, no numerals, no words, no captions, no subtitles, no UI labels, no signage, no logos, no watermarks, no moustached plumber, no red cap, no dungarees or overalls, no mushrooms, no turtles, no green pipes, no brick or question-mark blocks, no coins, no castle, no flagpole-and-castle ending, no Nintendo or any existing game's character, artwork or assets, no recognisable real person or celebrity, no firearm, no gore, no extra saturated colour.

identity_anchors.pg_owner: A pixel-art side-scroller hero 32 px tall: a man in his late forties, short salt-and-pepper hair, a light blue half-sleeve shirt worn untucked over dark grey trousers, brown sandals, and a fat bunch of keys on a ring at his right hip that swings behind him when he moves. No hat, no cap, no moustache, no gloves, no overalls, no boots. Flat 16-bit pixels, two-pixel dark outline, four flat shades per garment, no gradient and no anti-aliasing.
identity_anchors.the_ledger_level: A side-scrolling level whose platforms are the ruled rows of a paper rent register: cream-grey paper rows with faint blue rules and hand-written column marks, seen edge-on as solid ledges two pixels thick. The parallax behind is a desaturated four-storey PG building — grilled balconies, plastic water tanks on the roof, a washing line, an exposed stair — all graded toward grey. No brick blocks, no floating boxes, no pipes, no coins, no sky creatures.
identity_anchors.the_hazards: Five pixel hazards, each an object out of the owner's real month and never a creature: (1) a blank, unstamped ID form sheet that flutters in at head height; (2) a fat cash bundle that slides away along the row; (3) an open padlock travelling beside a bare steel cot frame; (4) a spike of paper slips and torn receipts skewered upright through the ledge; (5) a falling column of small bell icons. All in the same desaturated four-colour palette as the level, all moving on the horizontal.
identity_anchors.the_phone: A real, current, ordinary black slab smartphone held in a real adult human hand — photographic, not pixel art — with the RentOK app open on screen: a white app surface, a cyan #03FFF1 accent bar across the top, room-wise dues rows down the screen and one paid tick. The RentOK wordmark wherever it appears is the supplied logo file — 'Rent' in white and 'Ok' in cyan #03FFF1 on a blue #0038FF ground — placed, never redrawn, recoloured or regenerated.
identity_anchors.the_power_light: A cyan #03FFF1 light with two forms and no third: as a pixel aura it is a two-pixel cyan rim on the pg_owner plus a soft one-tile cyan bloom ahead of him; as real light it is the cyan spill thrown by the phone screen onto paper. It is the only saturated colour in the film and it is never a beam, a muzzle flash or a projectile.

hero_frame.description: A real hand holding a real phone a few centimetres above an open paper rent register, the RentOK app lit on the screen, its cyan light lying flat across the ruled page and picking the pen marks out warm-grey; at the right edge of that light, where the pixel world starts again, the paper spike and the falling bells are already coming apart into loose cyan grain. One frame, two worlds, the product in a working hand between them.

audio.music_bed: One continuous 16-bit chiptune cue laid by code across the whole 30 s, so it runs unbroken under every cut instead of restarting per clip. It is source music, not score: the scene is a game screen, so the chiptune has a visible origin inside the fiction and reads as the game's own sound rather than as commentary. It opens sparse and slightly grinding — a two-note bass loop and a tired arpeggio in the same key as the hits — which is exactly the register beats 1 to 3 keep, so the opening promises nothing the film fails to deliver. At 12.5 s it stops dead for the real-world insert, leaving one real haptic buzz and room tone as the bridge across worlds. At 17.0 s it returns a fifth higher and full-voiced, each cleared tile landing on a beat; at 22.0 s it resolves onto one held major chord as the last window lights, and does not loop again. No jingle, no lyric, no sung brand name and no mnemonic carries any part of the message — every point in the film survives with the sound off.

beats.title: The rent register turns into a level
beats.feeling: A PG owner's small private jolt of recognition — that is my book, my handwriting, my building — and then the unease of finding something alive in it. Not amusement yet; curiosity with a pulse under it.
beats.framing: 9:16. A worn rent register lies open on a steel desk, shot straight down and filling the lower two-thirds; a real thumb pins the left page at the very bottom edge of frame. The right page's ruled rows have already hardened into edge-on pixel ledges, and on the third ledge up — small, in the upper-middle zone — stands the pg_owner with his keys at his hip. Hard raking light from screen-left across the paper's tooth. In the clip the remaining rules quantise into ledges row by row from left to right, the desk edge slides out of the bottom of frame, and at 1.5 s the HUD bar assembles across the top: three lit life pips at the left, and at the far right one dark, unlit app tile with an empty slot in it. The supplied RentOK wordmark is composited small and unaltered at the HUD's top-left corner at the same moment.
beats.first_frame: One still that is half photograph and half video game: real ledger paper with real pen marks on the left, the identical ruled rows turned into solid pixel ledges on the right, one small pixel man standing on a ruled line as if it were a floor. No HUD, no on-screen words, no mark, no motion.
beats.impact: Locked camera, no move at all — the surprise is inside the frame, so nothing needs pointing at. The real paper rustle of the opening is cut off at 1.5 s by a single chiptune blip as the HUD lands, and the loop starts under it. Holds the full three seconds because the frame has two things to be read, paper and level, and both have to land before anything is asked of the viewer.

beats.title: Two hits before the tenth
beats.feeling: The flat, unglamorous grind of the first week of the month. He is quick and he is competent, and it still is not enough — the frustration belongs to the system, never to him.
beats.framing: Side-on game camera, locked; the level scrolls right to left so the pg_owner holds the left-of-centre zone and travels rightward for the whole film. He runs along the second ledger row. At 3.6 s a blank unstamped ID form sheet flutters in from screen-right at head height and he ducks under it without breaking stride. At 5.6 s a fat cash bundle sits waiting on the row ahead; he reaches, and it slides away from his fingers along the row and off the right edge. Behind him the desaturated PG building scrolls past — balcony grilles, water tanks, a washing line. One life pip goes dark at 6.2 s. The app tile at the HUD's right stays unlit.
beats.first_frame: The still at 3.0 s: the pg_owner mid-stride on a ledger row, both feet clear of the paper, keys lifted behind him; the blank ID form just entering the frame at the top right with one corner inside it; the cash bundle already visible further along the same row. Three life pips lit, app tile dark.
beats.impact: One cue for the beat and one only: hazards arrive on the horizontal and he never changes level, so the eye stays on a single line and the frame never competes with itself. The duck is silent; the cash slide gets the beat's only sound accent, a descending two-note chiptune slur, so the loss is heard rather than shown twice. No slapstick — he does not trip, stumble or gurn; the objects leave, he stays.

beats.title: Pinned, one pip left
beats.feeling: The specific late-month feeling of three things landing at once. Not panic — the flatter thing underneath it: the month has beaten him again and he can see exactly how.
beats.framing: Same row, same direction, same lock. At 8.3 s an open padlock and a bare steel cot frame slide fast along his row from behind and overtake him — a room emptied with nobody in it. At 9.9 s the ledge ahead sprouts a spike of paper slips and torn receipts skewered upright, blocking the row. At 11.3 s a column of small bell icons drops from the top of frame onto the ledge behind him. He is boxed: slips ahead, bells behind, a two-row drop below. He brakes and stops. The last life pip flashes. The unlit app tile at the HUD's right is now the only element on screen that has not been used.
beats.first_frame: The still at 8.0 s: the pg_owner braked to a standstill mid-row, one hand out for balance, knees bent; the open padlock and the empty cot frame level with his shoulder and already past him; the paper spike ahead breaking the top line of the ledge. Two pips lit, one dark, app tile dark.
beats.impact: The camera still does not move; the hazards do all the work, which is what keeps him competent rather than clumsy. The gap opened at 1.5 s narrows to a point here — everything on screen has now been spent except that one dark tile, so the viewer is asking the film's question for it. The music thins to the bass loop alone and the bells land off the beat, so the last 1.2 s read as a stall rather than a climax.

beats.title: The cheat code
beats.feeling: Relief that arrives as something physical and ordinary — a real hand, a real phone, real light falling on paper. The register drops out of the game for four and a half seconds and the room comes back.
beats.framing: Hard cut out of the level into the real world. A tight insert at a low three-quarter angle across the desk, lens close: a real hand holds the phone a few centimetres above the open rent register, RentOK open on screen — white surface, cyan #03FFF1 accent bar, room-wise dues rows, one paid tick. The phone is the only lit object; its cyan spill lies across the ruled page and picks the pen marks out warm-grey. At the right edge of the spill, where the pixel world resumes, the paper spike and the falling bells are already softening into loose cyan grain. The HUD's cheat-entry field lights at 13.4 s across the top of frame and takes INSTALL, then RENTOK APP.
beats.first_frame: The still at 12.5 s, before anything moves: real hand, real phone held over the real register, the RentOK app open and lit, cyan light lying flat across the ruled page, and at the far right of that light two pixel hazards caught mid-dissolve into cyan grain. Nothing else in the frame is saturated.
beats.impact: The chiptune stops dead on the cut; for 0.9 s the only sound is one real haptic buzz and the room's own tone, and that sound is what motivates the jump between two worlds. The camera holds absolutely still while the thumb makes one short scroll down the dues list — the product performs on camera, in a working hand, before anything is claimed for it. Holds the full 4.5 s: this is the frame that has to be read rather than glimpsed, and it is the closer shot that ties cyan to the product before cyan has to work small and fast in beat 5.

beats.title: Immunity, and the rows close
beats.feeling: The uncomplicated pleasure of a fair fight finally going your way. Earned, not gifted — he does the walking, the tool does the clearing.
beats.framing: Cut back into the level on the same row, same left-to-right travel. The pg_owner now carries the two-pixel cyan rim and a one-tile cyan bloom ahead of him, and a pixel phone is in his raised hand. He walks — he does not sprint — into the spike of slips, and the light reaches each hazard in turn. None of them explodes: each one it touches snaps square and locks down into the ledger row beneath as a filled cyan tile, and the completed row runs on ahead of him. The five tiles take ✓ DIGITAL KYC, ✓ AUTOPAY, ✓ DUES TRACKED LIVE, ✓ ONE DASHBOARD and ✓ COMPLAINT TICKETS, each landing in the exact screen position its problem label held in beats 2 and 3. The falling bells strike him and bounce off. The HUD's app tile is lit cyan and all three life pips are back.
beats.first_frame: The still at 17.0 s: the pg_owner stepping forward rimmed in cyan with the phone up, the paper spike a body's length ahead of him and its nearest slip already squaring into a cyan tile at the row line. Everything outside the bloom is the same dusty grey it has been since 0 s.
beats.impact: Declared action passage: the five conversions land about 0.8 s apart, faster than a shot that must be read would normally hold, and this is the one place in the film that licence is taken. He walks while everything around him accelerates — the contrast is what reads as power, not the speed. The chiptune returns a fifth higher on the cut and each tile lands on a beat, so the music channels a feeling the picture has already made instead of supplying one. Composition is declared restless here and nowhere else.

beats.title: The flag on his own roof
beats.feeling: Quiet ownership. The month is his again and the building is full — the feeling is the building, not the man's face.
beats.framing: The level's end is the PG's own rooftop. The flagpole is the building's existing TV-aerial mast and the flag is a plain cyan pennant with no mark on it. He puts a hand to the mast and the pennant runs up. As it climbs, the camera lifts with it along the frame's long axis, and the four storeys below come up window by window from the bottom — each shutter opening on a low warm-grey light behind it, until every room in the building is lit. The building's grey lifts about a stop; nothing but the pennant gains any saturation. The HUD has gone.
beats.first_frame: The still at 22.0 s: the pg_owner at the foot of the aerial mast on the rooftop ledge, hand already on it, the cyan pennant furled at the bottom of the pole; the four storeys of windows below him all dark; the top of the frame clean, with the HUD cleared away.
beats.impact: The only camera move in the film, and it is motivated by an object in transit — the flag takes the frame up with it. That move is also what makes the vertical format read as tall: the pennant at the top end of the long axis against the lit windows at the bottom end, rather than the 9:16 frame being asked to supply tallness by itself. The music resolves onto one held major chord as the last window lights and the loop does not restart; two beats of stillness at the top before the cut.

beats.title: Brand close, composed not generated
beats.feeling: Nothing performed. A plain instruction from a brand that has just spent twenty-seven seconds showing its work.
beats.framing: No generation at all: a code-composed card on a flat RentOK blue #0038FF ground. The supplied RentOK wordmark file sits unaltered in the upper third, at the top end of the long axis. Centred beneath it, a real still photograph of the phone with the RentOK app open — the same phone and the same screen as beat 4. Below that, INSTALL RENTOK APP set as one line in a medium-weight sans; RENTOK.COM small at the bottom end of the long axis. The cyan pennant is gone; the only cyan left on screen is the 'Ok' of the wordmark and the app's accent bar.
beats.first_frame: The card, complete and static from its first frame: blue ground, wordmark above, the real phone with the app open in the middle, the ask under it, the URL at the foot.
beats.impact: clip_s 0 — this beat is composited, never generated, so every letterform on it is real text and the mark is the supplied file rather than a rendering of one. The chiptune has already resolved; the card carries only the tail of that chord and then silence, which is also what the film sounds like on a muted feed. The last thing on screen is the product, not the game.

sources._note_no_other_text: These fifteen are the only legible words in the film. Nothing else is written, and none of them may claim a decoration exemption, because each was chosen because it is that word and could not be swapped for another without changing its purpose — so all fifteen are composed by code as real text and none is generated into pixels. The RentOK wordmark is not a string: it is the supplied logo file, placed unaltered.
sources._note_all_caps: Every supplied value is capitalised with may_reflow false. Each is a one-to-three-word label, never a running line, so the all-caps reading penalty is accepted at label length only; recorded in deviations.

hazard_label_1.why: Rides the blank ID form as it crosses, so the word names the object the viewer is already looking at rather than floating free. Set white #FFFFFF on a solid dark slate #1B1E24 label plate, about 15:1 at both the darkest and lightest point of that plate, because the pixel ground behind it is a moving, variable surface that cannot be measured. Held inside the Reels/Shorts vertical safe zone — clear of the top 12% and bottom 25% where the platforms put their own UI.

hazard_label_2.why: Sits on the cash bundle and slides off the frame with it, so the loss and its name leave together. Same plate and same measured ratio; same safe zone; same screen position family as its clear (s09) will later occupy.

hazard_label_3.why: Travels with the padlock and the empty cot, so the label reads as a caption on an event rather than a claim about the owner. Same plate, same ratio, same safe zone.

hazard_label_4.why: Pinned to the paper spike that blocks the row — the only hazard that stops him, so its label holds still while the other four move. Same plate, same ratio.

hazard_label_5.why: Falls with the column of bells and lands with them, the last word before the cut out of the game. Same plate, same ratio. Five labels, five positions, each of which its matching clear will reoccupy exactly.

cheat_entry.why: The cheat-code field at the top of the HUD, typed on in two steps 0.6 s apart so the instruction is read as an action being performed, not a super being shown. White #FFFFFF on a near-black #101318 field, about 18:1. This is the brief's cheat code and it is deliberately identical in wording to the closing ask, so the ask has already been rehearsed once by the time it is made.

cleared_tiles.why: Each string is composed into the cyan tile that replaces the problem it clears, landing about 0.8 s apart in the exact screen positions s03–s07 held, so the swap is legible without anyone explaining it. Set near-black #0B1F1E on cyan #03FFF1, about 16:1 — the highest-contrast pairing in the film, because these are the five load-bearing product facts and they get the shortest holds.

brand_close_card.why: The ask card. s13+s14 set as one line, white #FFFFFF on RentOK blue #0038FF, about 9.5:1; s15 set smaller in cyan #03FFF1 on the same blue, about 7.4:1, at the bottom end of the long axis opposite the wordmark at the top. The supplied wordmark sits between them untouched and takes the brand's own contrast, never an author-chosen recolour. Everything is held inside the vertical safe zone so a Reels caption strip or a Shorts subscribe bar cannot cover the ask.

mandatory.customer_words: "The video has a Mario game." … "Game identity: An original Mario-inspired game, rather than an exact reproduction of Nintendo's character, artwork, music or game assets."
mandatory.realisation: The whole film is one 16-bit side-scrolling level, so the form is unmistakably the one the customer asked for. Nothing in it is Nintendo's: the hero is a middle-aged man in a half-sleeve shirt with a keyring, the platforms are the ruled rows of a rent register, the hazards are paperwork and a padlock, the music is an original chiptune cue and the ending is a rooftop aerial mast, not a castle. The negative line bans the whole recognisable set — cap, moustache, dungarees, mushrooms, turtles, pipes, question-mark blocks, coins, castle — from every prompt.

mandatory.customer_words: "The player is basically a PG owner."
mandatory.realisation: The playable figure is the pg_owner anchor and he is on screen in every generated beat. He is the story's hero throughout; the brand never acts except in his hand. The buyer this film is written for is named from variables rather than as 'India': the owner-operator of a single 20-to-80-bed paying-guest property in a tier-1 or tier-2 city letting to migrant workers and students, who keeps a paper register, collects in person, and turns his month on the first.

Hazard 1, beat 2 at 3.6 s: a blank, unstamped ID form sheet flutters across at head height and he ducks it. Labelled TENANT VERIFICATION (s03); cleared by ✓ DIGITAL KYC (s08) in the same screen position at beat 5.
Hazard 2, beat 2 at 5.6 s: a cash bundle slides away from his reaching hand and off the frame, and a life pip goes dark. Labelled COLLECTING RENT (s04); cleared by ✓ AUTOPAY (s09).

Hazard 3, beat 3 at 8.3 s: an open padlock and a bare steel cot frame overtake him along the row — a room emptied with nobody in it. Labelled LEFT WITHOUT PAYING (s05); cleared by ✓ DUES TRACKED LIVE (s10).

Hazard 4, beat 3 at 9.9 s: a spike of paper slips and torn receipts skewered upright through the ledge — the only hazard that stops him dead, because it is the one that has no answer anywhere in his month. Labelled NO RECONCILIATION (s06); cleared by ✓ ONE DASHBOARD (s11).
Hazard 5, beat 3 at 11.3 s: a column of bell icons drops from the top of frame and boxes him in from behind. Labelled COMPLAINTS (s07); cleared by ✓ COMPLAINT TICKETS (s12).

mandatory.customer_words: "The game also introduces a cheat code — install RentOK app."
mandatory.realisation: Beat 4 is the cheat code and it is staged as a real action, not a super: the film cuts out of the level to a real hand and a real phone with the app open, and the HUD's cheat-entry field types INSTALL then RENTOK APP in the customer's own words (s01, s02). The same two words come back as the closing ask at 27.0 s (s13, s14), so the instruction is rehearsed inside the story before it is made of the viewer.

mandatory.customer_words: "Once it is done, Mario gets a gun sort of power/immunity."
mandatory.realisation: The immunity is literal and shown twice: at beat 5 the falling bells strike him and bounce off, and all three life pips come back. The 'gun sort of power' is delivered as a forward-reaching cyan light from the phone in his raised hand rather than as a firearm — the mechanic the customer asked for is preserved in full, the weapon is not. Recorded openly in deviations under the brief's own delegation of power-up design.

mandatory.customer_words: "It runs and kills all the obstacles"
mandatory.realisation: All five obstacles are cleared on screen in beat 5, in the order they were met, each in about 0.8 s. They do not explode: each one snaps square and locks into the ledger row beneath it as a completed cyan tile, so 'killing the obstacle' and 'closing the row' are the same event — which is what the product actually does and what makes the exaggeration rest on a truth.

Beat 6: the level ends on the PG's own rooftop, the flagpole is the building's TV-aerial mast, and he raises a plain cyan pennant. As it goes up, the four storeys below light window by window — the flag is the win condition, the full building is what winning means.

mandatory.customer_words: "Platforms: Instagram Reels / Facebook and YouTube Shorts."
mandatory.realisation: 9:16 throughout; every composed string sits inside the vertical safe zone, clear of the top 12% and the bottom 25% where the platforms overlay captions, handles and subscribe bars. The film is built to be read with the sound off — no point anywhere depends on audio — and the close card is static for its full three seconds so it survives a scroll-past and an autoplay loop.
Exactly 30.0 s: seven contiguous beats, six generated clips totalling 27.0 s (3.0 / 5.0 / 4.5 / 4.5 / 5.0 / 5.0) plus a 3.0 s code-composed close at clip_s 0.

mandatory.customer_words: "Visual treatment: Delegated to the creative system."
mandatory.realisation: The treatment chosen and declared: flat 16-bit pixel art, two-pixel outline, four flat shades, no gradients; the whole world graded down to dusty concrete grey and faded ochre with cyan #03FFF1 as the single saturated element; one hard key from screen-left; locked camera everywhere except the one motivated lift in beat 6; and one real-world photographic insert at beat 4 so the product is seen as itself and not as a drawing of itself.

mandatory.customer_words: "Power-up design: Delegated to the creative system, while preserving the requested game-style power/immunity mechanic."
mandatory.realisation: The power-up is the cyan light of the app: a two-pixel cyan rim and a one-tile bloom ahead of the owner, thrown by the phone he holds up. It is never a beam, a muzzle flash or a projectile. It grants immunity (bells bounce off), it clears every obstacle, and it is the same cyan established in close-up on the real phone screen one beat earlier, so the colour reads instantly as the product rather than as a game effect.

mandatory.customer_words: "Brand and product source: Official RentOK website, https://rentok.com." Reference asset rentok_wordmark, source/rentok-brand/rentok-new-logo.webp.
mandatory.realisation: The mark on screen is the supplied .webp file, placed and never redrawn, recoloured or regenerated — small in the HUD corner from 1.5 s and full size on the close card. The product on screen is the RentOK app itself, shown on a real phone at beat 4 and again on the close card. The URL is carried verbatim as RENTOK.COM (s15).

mandatory.customer_words: identity_invariants: "Rent in white", "Ok in cyan #03FFF1", "blue #0038FF ground".
mandatory.realisation: All three hold wherever the mark appears, because the mark is the supplied file rather than a rendering. The two brand values are also load-bearing elsewhere: cyan #03FFF1 is the film's one saturated colour and its power-up, and blue #0038FF is the ground of the close card. Delivered brand pixels are to be measured in context after grade, not accepted by name.

mandatory.customer_words: exact_text_strings — fifteen values, placement "overlay", script "latin", "may_reflow": false.
mandatory.realisation: All fifteen appear, verbatim, with no reflow, no line-breaking and no case change, composed by code into the finished frames. No other words appear anywhere in the film, and the prompts quote none of them — the negative line bans every letterform from generation, so no message word can exist only as generated pixels.

mandatory.customer_words: deliverable_request: aspect "9:16", count 1, kind "multi_shot_story", modality "video", motion from "generated", audio true, seconds 30, operation "generate".
mandatory.realisation: One 9:16 film, 30 s, multi-shot: a still generated per beat, image-to-video per beat, stitched by code, with a single continuous audio track laid by code over the stitch. The ambiguity marker is acknowledged rather than hidden — at 30 s this sits above the registered multi_shot_story band, so the structure is carried by six generated clips of 3.0–5.0 s each plus a composed close, which is the shape that band supports.

brand_timeline.in_context: The supplied RentOK wordmark rides the game HUD's top-left corner from 1.5 s to 22.0 s at a small constant size, unaltered, the way a sponsor's mark rides a real game screen — so the film is attributed from its second second rather than from its twelfth, and there is no lapse anywhere between 1.5 s and 30.0 s. The product itself enters in context at 12.5 s as the app open on a real phone in a real hand over the owner's own register, returns as the pixel phone in his hand through beat 5, and is the last thing on screen at 30.0 s. Branding therefore starts as a mix (mark, HUD app tile, the product's colour) and finishes on the product alone.
brand_timeline.spoken: none — the job's standing constraint forbids dialogue and voice-over, so the brand name is never said. It is shown instead: the mark from 1.5 s, the app on screen from 12.5 s, and the name composed as RENTOK APP at 13.4 s and again at 27.0 s. Declared as a deviation, because the doctrine default is to say the name as well as show it.

last_frame: The composed close card at 30.0 s, held static: flat RentOK blue #0038FF, the supplied wordmark unaltered at the top of the long axis, the real phone with the RentOK app open centred beneath it, INSTALL RENTOK APP under that, RENTOK.COM small at the foot. The film ends on the product, not on the game.

deviations.from: / default: set out to be interesting rather than funny, register follows product and audience, and a cartoon register for adults is below average (ogx_0038, ogx_0032, whip_0058) — humour and pastiche only on a brief clause.
deviations.brief_clause: "I want to make a video for RentOK.
